observed_facts: register_forward_hook and register_forward_pre_hook expose module boundaries; hooks can return replacement outputs.
PyTorch does not promise complete reproducibility across releases, platforms or CPU/GPU; deterministic algorithms can cost performance.
Inference/no-grad modes exclude operations from a backward graph; activation gradients require relevant differentiable inputs.
Upstream license has three redistribution conditions including non-endorsement. GitHub automatic SPDX classification returned NOASSERTION.
Selected-release upstream LICENSE matches observed v2.14.1 LICENSE SHA256.
Qwen3DecoderLayer returns hidden_states as a Tensor after both residual additions. Dense causal model decoder layer paths are model.layers.
Native Qwen3.5 implementation exists in v5.19.0; hybrid state handling differs from dense Qwen3.
Hybrid stack combines Gated DeltaNet linear attention and full attention; optional fast kernels have a PyTorch fallback.
Incremental decoding reuses internal cached states; masks and positions require alignment with the full sequence.
Local model tracing exposes activation save/edit operations; an additional tracing runtime is required.
v0.8.0.rc1 published 2026-09-09T20:53:05Z is explicitly prerelease; its execution engine is rewritten.
TransformerBridge is recommended, preserves raw HF weights by default, and optionally enables compatibility mode; legacy HookedTransformer.from_pretrained was removed in v4.0.
Dense Qwen3 architecture adapter is present.
Qwen3.5 hybrid adapter treats attention components as optional per layer and accounts for RMSNorm offset; dense text-only adapter rejects multimodal wrappers.
LFM2 adapter includes short convolution and attention components; first layer may be convolution, so dense attention assumptions are invalid.
Working maintainer-linked migration guide is migrating_to_v4.html.
Intervention configuration/model abstractions support interchange and trainable interventions.
Tagged constants inspected; dedicated Qwen3/hybrid support was not established by this file.
Tagged released Qwen mapping is explicitly for Qwen2 module classes. A similar module path does not certify Qwen3 support.
Current requirements explicitly include NVIDIA compute capability 7.5 and RTX20xx. Compiled binaries depend on Torch/CUDA build combination.
Attention backends have distinct hardware and feature support; general engine support does not certify a particular kernel.
Reproducibility requires attention to random seeds, scheduling and execution configuration; serving output is not a cross-engine bitwise identity guarantee.
Model architecture support is documented separately from hardware and attention-backend support.
Current installation offers compiled serving dependencies; this page does not independently establish a complete validated SM75 configuration.
Contributor RFC proposed SM75 deprecation in v0.5; issue closed 2025-07-17. An RFC and closure are not proof of final support policy.
Tagged build documentation supports GGML_CUDA and CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES selection. A build target of 75 is proposed, not executed.
Tagged server documents F16 K/V cache selection, no-context-shift, no-cache-prompt and chat-template-kwargs.
Generation in GGUF/C++ is a separate backend and numerical condition from HF eager instrumentation.
Explicit PyTorch indexes and package source mappings can select CPU/CUDA wheel families.
uv automatically resolves/syncs unless controlled; --locked rejects stale lock metadata, while --frozen bypasses freshness checks.
MIT license is present in uv 0.13.0.
Apache-2.0 license is present in uv 0.13.0; dual license is also publisher-declared.
Tensor serialization format stores a JSON header and tensor byte buffers rather than Python pickle objects.
Apache-2.0 license is present in v0.8.0.
allow_nan=False rejects nonfinite floats; object_pairs_hook permits explicit duplicate-key checking.
Standard-library logging provides local handlers and formatters; structured run-record fields remain a project responsibility.
Hydra provides hierarchical configuration composition and command-line overrides.
Pydantic models provide typed validation; coercion/strictness must be configured deliberately.
MLflow provides experiment, run, metric and artifact tracking; it is optional for the small local increment.
W&B run tracking is an optional additional dependency and synchronization policy, not selected for this increment.
Turing is compute capability 7.5 with FP16 Tensor Core multiplication and FP16/FP32 accumulation.
GPU catalog endpoint accessed; it was not used to assert a specific listed RTX2080Ti row.
Mainstream FlashAttention-2 NVIDIA support targets Ampere/Ada/Hopper; maintainer links a separate Turing subset implementation. BF16 requires newer architecture.
